summary: 14-day Nightscout telemetry demonstrates outstanding glycemic control with a Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL) of 99.7%, average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%), and zero clinical hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL). Active AAPS profile settings (basal, CR, ISF, DIA) and loop automation parameters are highly effective and well-matched to physiological needs. A minor postprandial peak (up to 188 mg/dL) during weekend brunches is easily managed by optimizing prebolus timing rather than altering core profile parameters.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM data completeness and cadence are ideal over the 14-day period, fully supporting downstream analytical inferences.
analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 valid entries out of 1,345 expected (100.0% coverage); 15.0-minute cadence; 0 data gaps; largest gap 15.0 minutes; 32 treatment logs.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic patterns demonstrate excellent safety with zero time below range (<70 mg/dL) and minimal time above range (>180 mg/dL).
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose 117.0 mg/dL; SD 15.1 mg/dL; CV 12.9%; Time in Range 99.7%; TAR 0.3%; TBR 0.0%. Lowest recorded values were 70-71 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight and fasting basal rates maintain glucose consistently within target ranges (90-110 mg/dL) without driving nocturnal hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Mean hourly local glucose between 00:00 and 06:00 ranges from 102.3 mg/dL to 112.9 mg/dL. Transient nocturnal dips to 70-71 mg/dL occurred on only two isolated nights at 03:00 UTC.

analysis_steps.findings: Carbohydrate ratios, Sensitivity Factors, and Duration of Insulin Action (5.5h) appropriately cover meals and restore baseline glucose within 4 hours.
analysis_steps.evidence: Postprandial glucose returns to start levels (100-125 mg/dL) by 240 minutes across all recurring meal windows (breakfast, brunch, dinner).

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM settings operate safely, providing effective micro-bolus assistance during meal absorption without causing insulin stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: Core switches smb_enabled=true and uam_enabled=true; smb_interval=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min.
data_gaps: Specific raw SMB activation flags (smb_always_enabled, smb_with_cob_enabled, etc.) are null in exported settings.

analysis_steps.findings: AAPS safety caps (max basal 2.4 U/h, max IOB 8.0 U) provide sufficient guardrails relative to Total Daily Insulin while permitting full loop operation.
analysis_steps.evidence: Max basal of 2.4 U/h is ~2.5x scheduled basal; max IOB of 8.0 U is ~1.4x largest meal bolus. Low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%) confirms limits prevent runaway delivery.
data_gaps: Autosens and Dynamic Sensitivity switch states are null in raw exported payload.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared meal bolus timing (prebolus 10-20 min, immediate bolus 60-70%) successfully controls postmeal excursions across breakfast, brunch, and dinner.
analysis_steps.evidence: 28 meal boluses analyzed. Weekday breakfast (20-min prebolus, 70% immediate) peaks at <168 mg/dL; dinner peaks at <140 mg/dL; all resolve by 240 min.

analysis_steps.findings: Weekend brunch e-carbs declaration (20g over 120 min) matches mixed-meal absorption, preventing late postprandial hyperglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Brunch 2-hour peak reaches 188 mg/dL (+62 to +70 mg/dL rise) but smoothly settles to 115-119 mg/dL by 240 minutes without correction boluses.

analysis_steps.findings: Synthesized analysis confirms that all core profile and AAPS parameters are optimal. No profile parameter changes are recommended. A minor adjustment to prebolus lead time for weekend brunches addresses transient postmeal peaks.
analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 99.7%, CV 12.9%, 0% hypoglycemia, robust recovery across all 28 logged meal windows over 14 days.

strengths: Exceptional overall glycemic control with 99.7% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL).
Zero time spent in hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) over 14 days of continuous monitoring.
Very low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%), well below the clinical stability target of 36%.
Accurate basal profile maintaining stable overnight glucose (mean 102-113 mg/dL).
Effective meal bolus strategies ensuring 4-hour postprandial resolution across all meal types.
issues: Transient postprandial peak reaching 188 mg/dL during high-fat/mixed weekend brunches due to a short 10-minute prebolus lead time.

recommendations.title: Extend Weekend Brunch Prebolus Lead Time
recommendations.description: Weekend brunches show a 2-hour postprandial excursion up to 188 mg/dL (+62 to +70 mg/dL above baseline) before returning smoothly to 115-119 mg/dL by 4 hours. Extending the prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes will better synchronize early insulin action with fast carbohydrate absorption without altering CR or basal settings.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all profile parameters (basal rates, CR, ISF, DIA) unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Current profile settings maintain 99.7% Time in Range, 12.9% CV, and zero time below 70 mg/dL. All meal windows resolve cleanly within 4 hours.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Re-evaluate 2-hour postprandial glucose peaks during weekend brunches after testing a 15-20 minute prebolus lead time.

parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Administer meal boluses 15-20 minutes before meals with 70% immediate bolus for standard meals, while allowing active SMB/UAM micro-dosing to smooth remaining postprandial curves.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Current timing achieves complete 4-hour postprandial resolution across all meal windows while maintaining 99.7% Time in Range.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Monitor 2-hour postprandial glucose peaks during weekend brunches after extending prebolus timing from 10 to 15-20 minutes.

exceptions.suggestion: Increase prebolus lead time from 10 to 15-20 minutes, giving 60% upfront bolus and 20g e-carbs over 120 minutes.
exceptions.rationale: Blunts the initial 2-hour excursion (currently peaking at 188 mg/dL) while e-carbs and SMBs safely prevent late postmeal spikes.

implementation_steps: Verify that active profile parameters and AAPS settings match the validated values in your pump and AAPS app.
Maintain all current basal rates, carb ratios, ISF values, DIA, and safety limits without alteration.
For weekend brunches, test extending your prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes prior to eating.
Observe 2-hour and 4-hour postprandial glucose levels over the next 2-3 weekend brunch occasions to evaluate peak reduction.
education: Prebolus timing allows rapid-acting insulin to begin working at the same time absorbed carbohydrates enter the bloodstream, reducing early postprandial peaks.
Extended carbohydrates (e-carbs) inform closed-loop algorithms of slow, delayed carbohydrate absorption typical of high-fat or high-protein meals without delivering excessive upfront insulin.
safety_notes: Decision-support content only. Independently verify all settings with your healthcare team.
Make changes one at a time and monitor glucose closely following any adjustment.
Never alter core safety caps or basal rates without consulting your diabetes care team.
